items.text: First-choice striker Kai Havertz strained a hamstring on Germany duty v Netherlands (24 Sep); back at Arsenal for treatment and doubtful for Leeds.
Captain Martin Odegaard took an ankle knock for Norway v Portugal (27 Sep); missed training but pain easing, expected back for Leeds.
Declan Rice withdrew from England to manage a neural hamstring issue carried since the World Cup; described as precautionary, not an acute injury.
Ezri Konsa picked up a minor issue on England duty and faced a late fitness test before the Czechia game.
William Saliba (back) remains out, with December now seen as his possible comeback window.
Ben White (groin), Cristhian Mosquera (thigh) and Piero Hincapie (muscular) could be available after the break; none started the Brighton loss.
Summer signings Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Christos Tzolis are bedding in as starters; ex-Leeds keeper Illan Meslier arrived on a free.
Beaten 3-0 at Brighton on 19 Sep, their first defeat of the season; sit 3 points behind leaders Man City, who have won all five.
Summer signing Harry Wilson (quad) missed the Palace draw and Wales duty; Farke hopes to have him back after the break, not yet confirmed fit.
Centre-back Joe Rodon (hamstring, hurt 30 Aug v Brentford) is still out on an 8-10 week layoff; striker Mateo Joseph (ACL) is out until 2027.
Ilia Gruev is back from April's knee injury and played 90 minutes for Bulgaria; an option for the third midfield slot.
Noah Okafor withdrew from Switzerland duty amid issues with coach Murat Yakin and stayed at Leeds to train.
Unbeaten in five league games (2W 3D) and 5th despite a flat 0-0 with Palace; Arsenal away is billed as their toughest test yet.
No injuries reported from Leeds' internationals; James Trafford started England's 2-0 win in Czechia and Nico Elvedi scored for Switzerland.

epl_2026-10-10_Arsenal_Leeds.summary: Arsenal (2nd) return from the break after a 3-0 loss at Brighton, their first defeat, with first-choice striker Kai Havertz doubtful (hamstring on Germany duty); Odegaard's ankle knock and Rice's hamstring management look minor and Saliba is still out. Leeds (5th) are unbeaten in five under Farke and hope to have Harry Wilson back, but still lack Joe Rodon. Ex-Leeds keeper Meslier is now at Arsenal.

items.text: Starting left-back Ian Maatsen is out 6-8 weeks with ankle tendon damage from the Forest loss (12 Sep); summer signing Matteo Ruggeri deputised.
Pau Torres (hamstring strain v Forest, not serious) missed the Spurs win but could be in contention for Brentford.
Free signing Leon Goretzka (knee) has yet to debut for Villa but is expected to be fit to feature against Brentford.
Amadou Onana (ACL) is out long-term; Marco Bizot, Brian Madjo and Alysson are also working back from knocks.
Summer rebuild: Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Emi Martinez left; ten arrivals include Nicolas Jackson and Johan Manzambi.
Unai Emery faced scrutiny after a winless four-game start (reports of internal talks if results kept sliding); eased by the 3-2 win at Spurs.
Captain Nathan Collins, off after 17 minutes v Sunderland with a calf strain and out for two games since, is expected back after the break.
Defender Sepp van den Berg, yet to play this season, is 'in a good place to come back after the international break', per Keith Andrews.
Mathias Jensen (minor issue) is expected back; winger Dango Ouattara, a bench option lately, missed Burkina Faso games through illness.
Unbeaten in seven in all competitions; the 3-0 win over Chelsea on 18 Sep was called their best performance of the season.
Kevin Schade (3 league goals) is in his best form under Andrews with contract talks ongoing; Igor Thiago was left out by Brazil but is backed by his coach.

Brentford (4th) are unbeaten under Keith Andrews after a 3-0 rout of Chelsea, have Kevin Schade in form and expect captain Nathan Collins back from a calf strain.

items.text: Top scorer Joao Pedro (3G, 3A) has a knee strain from the Hull draw; told to rest ~3.5 weeks from 18 Sep, so Bournemouth is touch and go.
Moises Caicedo (calf; just 14 minutes all season) is targeting a return against Bournemouth after the break.
Cole Palmer pulled out of England with a minor muscle problem; not thought serious, with Bournemouth the target for his return.
Reece James (hamstring) missed the Brentford loss and England duty but is aiming to be fit for Bournemouth.
Summer signings Marco Palestra and Emmanuel Emegha have yet to debut; both are targeting the Bournemouth game.
Back-up keeper Mike Penders (quad) and unused winger Jamie Gittens (ankle, on crutches) were hurt on international duty.
Xabi Alonso's side are winless in three after the 3-0 loss at Brentford and have gone 22 league games without a clean sheet.
Justin Kluivert, who had started every league game, was injured at Real Sociedad (17 Sep), missed Liverpool and is out for 'some weeks'.
Eli Junior Kroupi (foot) and Julian Araujo (thigh) are out until November; Amine Adli and Veljko Milosavljevic are nearing returns.
David Brooks withdrew from the Wales squad through injury on 30 Sep; he was among the substitutes against Liverpool.
New boss Marco Rose is still without a league win (0W 3D 2L) after losing 1-0 to Liverpool; he says he is confident the points will come.
Won their first-ever major European game, 2-1 at Real Sociedad on 17 Sep; Rose: 'That's Bournemouth football.'
Summer centre-back signing Antonio Silva has settled fast; Rose says he looks like he has played in the Premier League for years.

Left-back Leif Davis is in form, with two goals and an assist in three league games before the Everton trip.
Alvaro Arbeloa, appointed after Marco Silva left for Benfica, is under pressure; Football Insider says Fulham have sounded out Thomas Frank.

Fulham (19th) are winless in five under Alvaro Arbeloa, and reports say the club has sounded out Thomas Frank, though draws with Liverpool and Man United showed resilience. Both squads are otherwise largely healthy.

items.text: Benjamin Sesko (recurring shin problem) missed the Fulham draw and withdrew from Slovenia duty; no return date given.
Patrick Dorgu hurt his hamstring after 30 minutes of Denmark v Wales and was sent home; a recurrence, very unlikely to face Spurs.
Noussair Mazraoui went off with a back problem for Morocco v Lesotho. That deepens the left-back shortage, with Shaw's fitness also a concern.
Captain Bruno Fernandes was left out of Portugal's squad v Norway. He had played through pain in his last three games; United are monitoring him.
Rashford (knock at Fulham) and Mainoo (load management) pulled out of England duty; both are expected to be available for Spurs.
De Ligt (back), Ugarte (knee surgery) and Heaton are still out; Amad Diallo is close to returning from a pre-season ankle injury.
Pressure is mounting on Michael Carrick: one league win in five, three defeats in seven games in all competitions, and a late equaliser needed at Fulham.
Summer signings Baleba, Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Darlow are already in the recent results; Hojlund, Casemiro and Sancho left.
Pedro Porro (hamstring, hurt v Aston Villa) is out for about a month. He is the only senior right-back, so Archie Gray is likely to deputise.
Dejan Kulusevski is back in full group training after 16 months out; Old Trafford is tipped as a possible first involvement.
Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert (both ACL) and Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle) are still out.
Kudus, back from an eight-month quad injury with four sub appearances, was released by Ghana to keep recovering at Spurs.
De Zerbi is the bookmakers' favourite for the next Premier League sacking after £300m+ of spending; Pochettino is being mentioned.
Bottom of the table with two goals in five league games, despite averaging 60.6% possession (third-highest in the league).
Summer signings Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Marmoush are already in the recent results, but the much-changed side has yet to click.

Striker Brian Brobbey strained a hamstring for the Netherlands v Germany (24 Sep) and was sent back to Sunderland for assessment.
Key midfielder Noah Sadiki limped off for DR Congo on 28 Sep; the knock is not thought to be serious.
Left-back Reinildo served his one-match ban (sent off v Arsenal) at Man City and is due back for Brighton.
Habib Diarra (hamstring) and Romaine Mundle (knee, out until around January) remain out; Omar Alderete played 90 mins for Paraguay and can cover.
One win in five (1W 1D 3L) and 14th; conceded five in a 5-3 defeat at Man City just before the break.
Striker Babis Kostoulas (4 goals, 3 assists in 8 games) needed stitches after a leg knock on Greece duty but is recovering well.
Mats Wieffer (knee), Jack Hinshelwood (missed six games), Yankuba Minteh and Femi Azeez are pushing to be available after the break.
Pascal Struijk (hamstring, went off late v Arsenal) is being assessed; captain Lewis Dunk's neck injury from training is 'nothing major'.
Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) has yet to feature this season; Evan Ferguson (ankle surgery) and Stefanos Tzimas (ACL setback) remain out.
Summer midfield signing Chema Andres has impressed and headed in the third goal in the 3-0 win over Arsenal.
3rd with the league's best goal difference (+11) after winning 5-0 at Coventry and beating Arsenal 3-0 in their last two league games.

items.text: Glasner reunion: the former Palace boss, who won the FA Cup, Conference League and Community Shield there, now manages Forest.
Star striker Jean-Philippe Mateta (hamstring, out since late August) may return after the break, but Sage calls him 'more uncertain'.
Captain and goalkeeper Dean Henderson (foot) is expected back after the break; Walter Benitez has deputised.
Axel Disasi serves the last game of a three-match ban for his straight red card v Ipswich on Sept 12.
Lerma (foot, 75%) and Tomiyasu (calf, 50%) are being assessed; Chadi Riad (knee) is out long-term.
New boss Pierre Sage's side kept their first clean sheet in a 0-0 at Leeds, after conceding 11 in their first four games.
Summer: centre-back Lacroix was sold to Chelsea; Disasi, Tomiyasu, Mingueza, McNeil and Khalaili were among the arrivals.
Centre-back Nikola Milenkovic (hamstring) missed Villa and Coventry; Premier Injuries lists Oct 11 as his expected return.
Right-back Nicolò Savona (knee) is still out after several setbacks.
Forest have failed to score in three straight home league games, a club first, but drew 2-2 at Liverpool and won 2-1 at Villa.
Glasner said he felt 'the heaviness of the past' after the 1-0 home defeat by promoted Coventry.
Summer: Forest signed Delap (£50m), Diomande, Ndoye and ex-Palace right-back Daniel Muñoz, and sold Elliot Anderson to Man City (£116m).

items.text: Tim Iroegbunam, signed from Everton, re-aggravated a groin injury and misses the reunion. He had yet to start a Premier League game.
Summer striker signing Ilyas Ansah (back) is due to see a specialist, and Hidemasa Morita is still working back from a pre-season injury.
Nobel Mendy (concussed v Chelsea) missed Newcastle; Jakirovic said he would then join up with his national team.
Left-back Matt Targett (ankle) is 50% and being assessed; goalkeeper Jack Butland (elbow surgery) is out until December.
Promoted Hull went unbeaten in their first four games (8 pts), including a 2-0 win over Man Utd, before losing at Newcastle.
Merlin Röhl, who started the first three games at right-back, is aiming for Hull; Maitland-Niles has since taken his place.
Christian Nørgaard is back in training. He has not played since his £7m move from Arsenal; Moyes calls him 'hugely important'.
Unbeaten in seven under Moyes after beating Ipswich 1-0, but they have scored only six goals from 60 chances in five league games.
Thin squad: only 18 first-team players, with Thierno Barry the lone senior centre-forward. Summer signing Hackney is settling in.

Regular left-winger Cody Gakpo hurt his ankle in a tackle v Serbia and left the Netherlands squad; he is being assessed.
Ekitike (Achilles), Bradley (knee) and Leoni (ACL) are still out; Chiesa (back) has a realistic chance of involvement.
Andoni Iraola is in his first season, appointed in June after Arne Slot was sacked.
Unbeaten in the league (W2 D3, 7-4 goals); Isak scored the winner at Bournemouth before the break.

Phil Foden serves the final game of a three-match ban for his derby red card (kicking out at Bruno Fernandes); he already missed Sunderland.
Antoine Semenyo withdrew from Ghana duty with an ankle/leg problem and is a major doubt.
Nico O'Reilly missed England's Czechia game with a minor issue; he had already lost his starting left-back spot to Gvardiol.
An independent commission found City guilty of serious Premier League financial breaches. Sanctions are pending and City plan to appeal.
Enzo Maresca replaced Guardiola, who resigned, in June. The £116m signing of Elliot Anderson from Forest is already in the side.
Perfect start: five league wins from five (13-5 goals) and top of the table.

Lampard expects Luke Woolfenden, Kaine Kesler-Hayden and Josh Eccles to be fit after the international break.
Full-back Milan van Ewijk (hamstring) is hoped to be back for Newcastle; Premier Injuries rates him 25%.

Joelinton (groin) trained with the senior group and is in line to face Coventry.
Dan Burn, Amar Dedić and Nico González, all absent v Hull, are expected back after the international break.

Fabian Schär was a new absence from training on Sept 29, with no reason given.
